source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 10 (questions: PDF pages 35-38, solutions: PDF pages 120-125). The pictures are cropped with tools/figures/ch10.json; questions that point back to an earlier question's figure (Q4-6, Q8-9, Q11) show that figure again and say "the figure". Every count is worked out from the shape, cube by cube, in tools/check_cubes_cutting.ts.

questions.prompt: In the given figure, a complete big cube is cut into small cube pieces. How many small cubes are there in the figure?
questions.rule: Each edge is cut into 3 equal parts, so there are 3 layers of 3 × 3 small cubes.

questions.prompt: In the given figure, a complete big cube is cut into small cube pieces and some of the small cubes are removed. How many small cubes are remaining after the removal, as shown in the figure?
questions.rule: Count layer by layer. The bottom layer is full (3 × 3); the two layers above it have 3 × 2 cubes each, because the front row is cut away.

questions.prompt: In the given figure, a complete big cube is cut into small cube pieces and some of the small cubes are removed. How many small cubes are remaining after the removal, as shown in the figure?
questions.rule: The cube is cut into 3 steps. Count layer by layer: each step down has one more row of 3 cubes.

questions.prompt: How many small cubes are cut and removed from the figure?
questions.rule: The full cube had 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 small cubes. Count what is missing in each layer.

questions.prompt: How many small cubes should be added to make the figure a complete cube?
questions.rule: The cubes to add are exactly the ones that were removed.

questions.prompt: In the figure, a complete big cube is cut into small cube pieces, each one measuring 1 cubic unit. Find the area of laminate sheet required to cover the given figure.
questions.rule: Each small cube face is 1 square unit. Count the faces seen from each of the six sides; for steps like these, every uncovered face is seen from exactly one side.
questions.working: Right 6 + left 6 + top 9 + bottom 9 + front 9 + back 9 = 48 square units

questions.prompt: In the given figure, a complete cube is cut into small cube pieces and some of the small cubes are removed. How many small cubes are remaining after the removal, as shown in the figure?
questions.rule: A 4 × 4 × 4 cube cut into 4 steps. Each layer down has one more row of 4 cubes.

questions.prompt: How many small cubes are cut and removed from the figure?
questions.rule: The full cube had 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 small cubes. Count what is missing in each layer.

questions.prompt: How many small cubes should be added to make the figure a complete cube?
questions.rule: The cubes to add are exactly the ones that were removed.

questions.prompt: In the given figure, a complete cube is cut into small cube pieces and some of the small cubes are removed. How many small cubes are remaining after the removal, as shown in the figure?
questions.rule: A 5 × 5 × 5 cube. The book counts 2 full rows of 5 left in the top layer, 4 rows in the next layer and full layers below.
questions.note: Hidden: the drawing can't be read clearly. The book's key (105) counts only 2 rows left in the top layer, but the picture also shows a third ridge of cubes on top, in the middle and set back from the front, and the groove in the second layer seems to stop behind the front. Read that way the count is not any option. Needs a check against a clearer copy of the figure.

questions.prompt: How many small cubes are cut and removed from the figure?
questions.rule: The book counts 3 rows of 5 removed from the top layer and 1 row of 5 from the second layer.
questions.note: Hidden: it uses the figure of Q10, which can't be read clearly (see Q10). The book's 20 needs 3 full rows missing from the top layer, but the picture seems to show a ridge of cubes still standing in the middle of the top.

questions.prompt: How many cubes are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: The pile stands in a corner, so every cube you see rests on cubes you can't see. Count each column from the top: 1, then 1 + 2, then 1 + 2 + 3, then 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.
questions.note: Only 10 cubes can be seen (option B). The book's answer, 20, also counts the hidden cubes each seen cube must rest on.

questions.prompt: Find the number of small cubes having edge length of 2 cm made by cutting a solid cube of edge length 8 cm.
questions.rule: Each edge of 8 cm gives 8 ÷ 2 = 4 small cubes, so there are 4 × 4 × 4.

questions.prompt: Find the number of small cubes having edge length of 3 cm made by cutting a solid cube of edge length 15 cm.
questions.rule: Each edge of 15 cm gives 15 ÷ 3 = 5 small cubes, so there are 5 × 5 × 5.

questions.prompt: A big cube of 64 cubic units volume is cut into small cubes of 1 cubic unit each. Now a layer of small cubes, each having 1 cubic unit volume, is removed from each face of the big cube. Find the number of small cubes remaining after the removal.
questions.rule: 64 = 4³, so each edge is 4 cubes long. Taking a layer off both ends of each edge leaves 4 − 2 = 2.
